title: SAFT: Safety-Preserving Adaptation via Fine-Tuning Transfer for Large Language Models

problem.claim: Fine-tuning instruction-tuned large language models on imperfect downstream data can erode safety alignment.

gap.claim: Existing safety-preserving fine-tuning methods may destabilize refusal behaviors or limit task adaptation by imposing an alignment tax.

contributions.claim: SAFT decouples task learning from alignment preservation by learning a safety-guided task update on a paired pretrained base model, rectifying task gradients against a safety objective, and transferring the update to a frozen instruction model through parameter-space grafting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across mathematical reasoning, code generation, and medical question answering, SAFT improves downstream utility while maintaining low harmfulness under a unified evaluation protocol.
On Llama3.1-8B-Instruct and Gemma3-4B-IT, SAFT achieves better safety and utility trade-offs than nine baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Downstream adaptation can damage safety alignment when fine-tuning data is imperfect.
Prior safety-preserving approaches can destabilize refusals or restrict adaptation.
SAFT learns and safety-corrects task updates on a pretrained base model before grafting them into a frozen instruction model.
The authors report improved utility, low harmfulness, and better safety-utility trade-offs across three tasks, two model families, and nine baselines.

source_observation.claim: SAFT separates task adaptation from alignment preservation and transfers a safety-guided update into the instruction model.

interpretation.claim: Separating adaptation from preservation may reduce conflicts between downstream learning and safety behavior.

application.claim: For safety-sensitive model adaptation, consider learning task updates on a pretrained base model and applying safety-aware parameter transfer to an aligned model.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported tasks, model families, or evaluation protocol.

unknowns: No numerical utility or harmfulness results are provided.
The abstract does not specify the safety objective, gradient-rectification procedure, or parameter-space grafting details.
The abstract does not identify the nine baselines or provide independent verification.
